questions.q: Why does this capstone use three report pages instead of one?
options: Cramming regional performance, profitability, and fulfillment onto one page would violate the 'fit it to one screen' rule once real data replaces placeholders
Power BI only allows a maximum of one visual per page
Three pages are always required regardless of content
Each page must correspond to exactly one DAX measure
questions.explain: Chapter 8's one-screen rule breaks down with three requirement groups worth of visuals crammed together — three focused pages serve the audience better than one crowded one.

questions.q: Why does the Regional Performance page use a sorted bar chart rather than a map for the territory comparison?
options: A sorted bar chart is more honest for precise comparison than a map, per Chapter 7's distortion checklist
Power BI doesn't support map visuals
Bar charts are always required for territory data
Maps can only show a single data point at a time
questions.explain: Chapter 7 taught that some visual choices distort more than they clarify — for precise numeric comparison across territories, a sorted bar chart communicates more honestly than a map.

questions.q: On the Product Profitability page, why is the bar chart sorted by Gross Margin % descending rather than alphabetically?
options: Sorting by the metric itself surfaces the real story; alphabetical sorting would bury which categories actually drive margin
Alphabetical sorting is not technically possible in Power BI
Descending sort is required by Microsoft's design guidelines
It has no effect on what the viewer notices first
questions.explain: Sorting by the actual metric puts the most and least profitable categories where the eye lands first — alphabetical order would scatter that story randomly across the chart.

questions.q: Why should color and sort conventions be identical across all three report pages?
options: A viewer who learns the color coding on one page shouldn't have to relearn it on another — consistency was the point of Chapter 8's storytelling lesson
Power BI automatically enforces identical formatting across pages
It has no real effect on how the report is understood
Only the first page's formatting actually matters
questions.explain: Consistent visual language across pages is a core storytelling principle from Chapter 8 — it lets the viewer's learned expectations carry forward instead of resetting on every new page.

questions.q: What determines the headline card on each of this capstone's three pages?
options: The single most important number for that page's specific requirement group, placed top-left per Chapter 8's reading-order principle
Whichever visual happens to be built first
The visual with the most colors
A random selection made by Power BI automatically
questions.explain: Each page's headline card is deliberately chosen to be the number that matters most for that page's requirement (Total Sales, Gross Margin %, or Sales YoY %) and placed where the eye lands first.
